'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[ISIL insurgency in Iraq (2017–present)|ISIL insurgency in Iraq]]
**Eleven [[Popular Mobilization Forces]] members are killed, including a brigade commander, and ten others wounded in an [[ambush]] by suspected [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State]] militants east of [[Tikrit]]. [https://thearabweekly.com/supspected-isis-attack-kills-11-iraq-raises-questions-about-security (''The Arab Weekly'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
*****The [[University of Michigan]] shuts down all [[Michigan Wolverines|sports]] activities for two weeks after the B.1.1.7 variant of [[SARS-CoV-2]] is discovered in five people with ties to the school. [https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2021/01/michigan-athletics-to-shut-down-for-2-weeks-after-covid-19-outbreak.html (MLive.com)] [https://www.mlive.com/public-interest/2021/01/three-more-covid-19-variant-cases-identified-in-michigan-health-leaders-urge-testing.html (MLive.com<sup>2</sup>)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in North Carolina]], Variant of Concern 202012/01
*****[[North Carolina]] reports their first case of the B.1.1.7 variant of [[SARS-CoV-2]] in a person in [[Mecklenburg County, North Carolina|Mecklenburg County]]. [https://amp.newsobserver.com/news/coronavirus/article248385355.html (''Raleigh News and Observer'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
*****Federal officials announce that all indoor portions of the [[National Mall]] and memorial parks will be closed to the public to combat the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/indoor-portions-national-mall-closed-prevent-spread-covid-19-n1255443 (NBC News)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington (state)]], Variant of Concern 202012/01
*****[[Washington (state)|Washington]] reports their first cases of the B.1.1.7 variant of [[SARS-CoV-2]] in two people residing in [[Snohomish County, Washington|Snohomish County]]. [https://mynorthwest.com/2499046/first-cases-covid-uk-variant-washington/amp/ (MyNorthwest.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Brunswick]]
*****[[New Brunswick]]'s [[Edmundston]] region begins a 14-day [[lockdown]]. Non-essential travel is prohibited in and out of the area. In addition, all non-essential businesses, schools and public spaces are closed, and all indoor and outdoor gatherings among people of different households are prohibited. [https://www.thestar.com/news/canada/2021/01/23/14-day-lockdown-for-new-brunswicks-edmundston-region-begins-tonight.html (''The Toronto Star'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario]]
*****A teen in [[London, Ontario|London]], [[Ontario]], dies from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], making him the youngest person in the area to die from the disease. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/male-teen-long-term-care-home-worker-london-middlesex-1.5885490 (CBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 9,912 recoveries in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 791,059. [https://health.detik.com/berita-detikhealth/d-5345744/sebaran-rekor-9912-pasien-sembuh-covid-19-terbanyak-di-dki-jabar (detikHealth)]
****[[Indonesia|Indonesian]] [[Coronavirus Disease Response Acceleration Task Force|COVID-19 Task Force]] chairman and Chairman of the [[Indonesian National Board for Disaster Management|National Disaster Management Agency]] [[Doni Monardo]] announces that he has tested positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2021-01/23/c_139691975.htm (Xinhua)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]] surpasses 5,000 deaths from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/01/23/national/japan-coronavirus-jan23/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 4,275 new confirmed cases and 4,313 recoveries in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide totals to 180,455 confirmed cases and 137,019 recoveries. [https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2021/01/23/covid-19-malaysia-reports-record-high-daily-new-cases-and-recoveries-at-427/1943360 (''Malay Mail'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]]
****Health Minister [[Pavithra Wanniarachchi]] tests positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] after previously endorsing [[Witchcraft|sorcery]] and magic potions. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210123-sri-lankan-health-minister-tests-positive-for-covid-19-after-endorsing-sorcery (France 24)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Norway]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
****Health authorities impose tougher [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdowns]] in [[Oslo]] and nine neighbouring [[List of municipalities of Norway|municipalities]] due to an increase in cases of a [[Variant of Concern 202012/01|more contagious variant]] from the UK that also caused two deaths in care home residents yesterday. [https://www.vg.no/nyheter/innenriks/i/41Lm8o/ny-lockdown-i-oslo-regionen-strengeste-tiltak-siden-mars (VG)] [https://www.ft.com/content/e772b7c8-e835-4d2d-93a9-63489ca234ad (''Financial Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports a record 15,333 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 624,469. The country also reports a record 274 deaths in the past 24 hours, surpassing 10,000 deaths from COVID-19. [https://sicnoticias.pt/especiais/coronavirus/2021-01-23-Portugal-com-mais-274-mortes-e-15.333-novos-casos-de-covid-19-nas-ultimas-24-horas (SIC Notícias)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the military]]
****[[Chief of the Defence Staff (Spain)|Chief of the Defence Staff]] [[Miguel Ángel Villarroya]] resigns after he admitted to receiving a dose of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] while not being on the priority list. [https://www.sbs.com.au/news/spain-defence-chief-resigns-for-getting-vaccine-before-allowed (AFP via SBS News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] signs a deal with the [[Russian Direct Investment Fund]] for the production of its [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.dailysabah.com/turkey/russia-signs-deal-with-turkey-on-vaccine-production/news (''Daily Sabah'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt]], COVID-19 vaccine
****[[President of Egypt|President]] [[Abdel Fattah el-Sisi]] announces that the [[Egypt|country]] will begin vaccinations tomorrow. Medical staff will be the first to receive the vaccine. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-egypt-vaccinations-in/sisi-says-egypt-to-begin-covid-19-vaccinations-on-sunday-idUSKBN29S0MQ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia]]
****[[Tunisia]] bans gatherings including demonstrations and extends their curfew to between 8:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m. local time until February 14 in an attempt to reduce the spread of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/africa/tunisia-bans-protests-extends-curfew-as-virus-cases-jump/2021/01/23/e5b2e0de-5d8f-11eb-a849-6f9423a75ffd_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in Brazil]]
****[[Brazil]] begins distribution of the [[AstraZeneca]]-[[University of Oxford|Oxford University]] [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/535550-astrazeneca-vaccine-distribution-begins-in-brazil (''The Hill'')]
***[[Amazonas (Brazilian state)|Amazonas]] Governor [[Wilson Lima]] announces new, tougher restrictions to curb the spread of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], beginning January 25. People will only be allowed to leave their homes for essential purposes such grocery shopping. [https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/amp/nacional/2021/01/23/covid-19-governo-do-amazonas-anuncia-novas-restricoes-para-conter-pandemia (CNN Brasil)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Russian protests]], aftermath of the [[poisoning of Alexei Navalny]]
**Over 3,500 people are detained in [[Russia]] amid [[2021 Russian protests|nationwide protests]] in support of jailed opposition leader [[Alexei Navalny]]. [[Moscow]] officials say 29 people have received medical assistance in hospitals, while a female protester in [[Saint Petersburg]] is currently in [[Intensive care unit|intensive care]] after being kicked by a riot police officer. [https://www.dw.com/en/russia-police-detain-thousands-at-pro-navalny-protests/a-56321592 (DW)] [https://news.sky.com/story/alexei-navalny-supporters-clash-with-police-and-hundreds-arrested-as-mass-protests-expected-across-russia-12196130 (Sky News)] [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/01/24/kremlin-says-us-interfering-in-russian-domestic-affairs-a72710 (''The Moscow Times'')]
*[[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**Garret Miller, a [[Texas]] man who participated in the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|storming]] of the [[United States Capitol]], is charged for threatening to [[assassinate]] [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Rep.]] [[Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2021/jan/23/alexandria-ocasio-cortez-man-charged-threat (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Police brutality in the United States]]
**A [[Tacoma, Washington]] police officer drove through a downtown crowd, running over at least one person and sending them to the hospital. The officer was responding to calls that a group of people were blocking a downtown intersection when the crowd surrounded on the police car, [[Tacoma Police Department]] said. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/video-shows-tacoma-police-vehicle-drive-through-crowd-run-over-n1255452 (NBC)]
*[[Deforestation of the Amazon rainforest]]
**[[Indigenous peoples in Brazil|Brazilian indigenous]] leaders [[Raoni Metuktire]] of the [[Kayapo]] tribe and Almir Narayamoga Surui of the [[Paiter]] Surui tribe call for the [[International Criminal Court]] to investigate [[President of Brazil|President]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]] for "crimes against humanity" such as environmental damage to the [[Amazon rainforest]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20210123-brazil-indigenous-leaders-sue-bolsonaro-for-killings-and-ecological-destruction (France 24)]
